lead.message:
Here is what I understand: Weekend Trips is a small browser app, on desktop and phone, where a group of friends plans a weekend away. It covers three things: who is in, the day plan, and what it costs each person. The repository has no code, so nothing constrains the design yet.

I opened round 1 on the experience. The designer will make two variants of the trip home screen on desktop and phone. Both show who is in, the day plan and the cost per person. They differ in the main idea:
- Variant 1: one page with three sections (People, Plan, Costs).
- Variant 2: a day-by-day timeline, with people and costs attached to each day.

Assumptions (please correct any):
- One trip per group, shared by a link, with no account needed at first.
- Costs are split equally by default. The screen shows who owes what, but no payments happen in the app.
- Friends are mostly on phones. The organizer may use a desktop.

Questions for you are beside the round. I did not set the product domain. I recommend "screen", because people use this on a screen.

The vision draft is below. Accept, edit or dismiss it.

steps.name: designer runs asked for by the lead: a short idea

runs.brief:
Design the main trip screen for Weekend Trips, a small app where 3–8 friends plan a weekend away. It must show who is in (in/out/maybe), the day plan (Friday to Sunday items), and each person's cost share. Make 2 variants. Variant 1: one page with three sections (People, Plan, Costs). Variant 2: a day-by-day timeline where people and costs attach to each day. Show realistic sample data, including a person who is undecided. Phone first, with a desktop layout. Keep the core loop simple: see the status, add a plan item, see what I pay.

The lead asks for: screen; 2 variants side by side, differing in a real choice; for desktop, mobile.

steps.summary: As it is today: one static Trip board page with two hand-written trip cards (Lake weekend, City walk), a non-working "I'm in" button, and a responsive card grid. No script, no storage.

lead.message:
I read the code (index.html and style.css, no JavaScript). Here is what the app does today.

**As it is today**
- One static page titled "Trip board", with the line "The weekends we are planning."
- Two trip cards, written by hand in the HTML: "Lake weekend" (Sat 17 – Sun 18 Oct, Pine Lake cabin, 4 in: Ana, Jo, Kai, Sam, about $140 each) and "City walk" (Sat 31 Oct, Old town, 2 in: Ana, Kai, 3 not yet, about $35 each).
- Each card has an "I'm in" button. It does nothing, because the page has no script and no storage.
- The cards sit in a responsive grid (minimum 260px per card). There is one style: a warm grey background and white cards with a teal button.
- There is no way to add a trip, change a trip, or see the cost split. Nothing is saved.

**Round 0 (opened now)**
I asked the designer to reproduce the page from the code, one take for desktop and one for mobile. The PE checks only that it matches the code. Please correct anything that looks wrong. Later rounds will change it.

**Assumptions (to confirm)**
- The users are a small group of friends who plan weekends together.
- The main gap is that "I'm in" is not real, and the data is fixed in the HTML.

I did not ask a vision question yet, to keep this first reply short. Please tell me which change matters most to you. In the studio, I would suggest a "screen" product domain.

verdicts.reasons: The screen uses standard browser features and manual inputs; it needs no external data source. Its three sections fit a small group and a weekend, with columns on desktop and stacked sections on phones. Standard HTML, CSS and JavaScript support longevity without third-party dependencies. No required paid service appears, but budget compliance remains unverified: about $2.82 remains for building, and no full-product cost basis exists. I inspected the files and screenshots; I could not check live interactions, shared storage, hosting or operating costs. The mobile screenshot ends before Costs, so it does not verify that section visually.

openCases.text: Does attendance apply to the whole trip or separately to each day?
openCases.why: A uses trip attendance; B uses daily attendance. This choice determines the data model and cost calculation.

openCases.text: Should costs split equally among confirmed attendees, including lodging, or can each expense have different participants?
openCases.why: Both variants assume equal shares. Lodging and optional activities may need different allocation rules.

openCases.text: What should the screen show when nobody is confirmed, several people are undecided, or shares leave a remainder of cents?
openCases.why: The samples do not establish these rules. A can divide by zero, and both variants assume one undecided person in summary text.

openCases.text: Who can change attendance and plan items, and must changes persist and appear on other friends' devices?
openCases.why: The prototypes keep changes only in browser memory. Permissions, storage and synchronization affect implementation and budget.

openCases.text: Are the amounts planning estimates or actual expenses that track who paid?
openCases.why: The label 'You pay' implies an obligation, but neither sample records payments or balances.

verdicts.reasons: Daily attendance and daily cost totals are feasible with standard browser features and manual inputs. Three day cards fit the stated weekend and small-group scale; screenshots show desktop columns and a phone timeline. The design requires no external data source or third-party dependency, which supports longevity. Daily attendance adds data and calculation cases, but no evidence establishes a budget violation. Budget compliance remains unverified without a full-product cost basis or provider prices. I inspected files and screenshots, not live interactions or shared storage; the samples use different costs, so their totals cannot compare variant efficiency.

openCases.text: How should someone set the time for a new activity in B?
openCases.why: B shows timed activities but provides no time input. Its prototype assigns every new activity to noon.
